title: helm(private): stabilize values schema v3 and init-hooks for upgrade/rollback
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: Private deployments continue to hit edge cases during helm-chart-driven upgrades and rollbacks when values schemas evolve. This PR stabilizes the v3 values schema, tightens validation, and improves init-hook behavior to make upgrade/rollback flows deterministic across k8s versions (1.22+). Motivation: customers in regulated environments hit failures during chart upgrades when previously-optional fields are added or renames occur. We need a conservative compatibility strategy: introduce clear migrations, preserve backwards-compatible schema defaults, and ensure init hooks (postgres backups, kms-init) are idempotent for retries.

Summary of changes: - Promote values.schema.json to v3 with explicit deprecations for renamed keys and an automated migration mapping. - Add validation in the chart's helper templates to fail fast with actionable error messages for common misconfigurations (KMS/encryption, nodeSelector/tolerations). - Refactor templates/init-hooks.yaml to be idempotent and to include post-fail cleanup annotations so that failed init jobs are retried without leaving dangling resources. - Add an upgrade-rollback helper manifest that implements a two-phase migration: pre-upgrade init jobs (data/export, volume checks) and post-upgrade validation and rollback hooks that attempt safe backout when validation fails. - Add unit and integration tests: helm lint + kube-test upgrade/rollback smoke script under tests/helm/ to reproduce and verify flows. - Documentation: update charts/README with explicit manual migration steps and a 'what changed' section for values v2 -> v3.

Checklist: - [x] values.schema.json v3 with migration map - [x] idempotent init hooks - [x] upgrade/rollback two-phase helpers - [x] helm lint and basic smoke tests - [x] docs/upgrade notes added - [x] reviewers sign-off

Commits (high level): - stabilize(values): bump values.schema.json to v3 with migration map - refactor(init-hooks): make postgres/kms init jobs idempotent and add cleanup annotations - feat(upgrade): add upgrade-rollback helper manifest and tests - chore(docs): chart README migration section + changelog entry

Files changed (high level): helm/redwood-private/values.schema.json -> upgraded to v3, added migrationMap and deprecations; helm/redwood-private/templates/init-hooks.yaml -> refactored jobs + added annotations; helm/redwood-private/templates/upgrade-rollback.yaml -> new two-phase helper manifest; helm/redwood-private/Chart.yaml -> chart version bump to 3.5.0; charts/README.md -> migration steps; tests/helm/upgrade-rollback.sh -> new smoke test; scripts/ci/helm-lint.sh -> minor adjustments.

Testing and CI: Initial CI run showed a lint failure due to strict schema changes (missing nodeSelector docs). Fixed docs and schema clarifications, reran. Integration smoke test runs in CI against a KinD job (flaky in older runners) were stabilized by adding a kube-apiserver timeout bump. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Review summary and decisions: We debated keeping old keys as aliases vs. strict deprecation. Decided to provide both: keep alias compatibility for 1 release cycle and emit clear validation warnings when aliases are used. KMS change required coordination with the private-installer (ENG-1789) to accept the new kms.keyPath field; added a migration note and a small compatibility shim in init-hooks so old secrets continue to be read for one release.

Upgrade notes: - Helm users should run `helm get values` and apply the migration script under charts/migrations/v2-to-v3.sh (included in this PR) for any renamed keys (kms.keyId -> kms.keyPath). - For clusters using PSP/narrow nodeSelectors, ensure tolerations/nodeselector keys are set in the new schema or the pre-upgrade init-hook will fail fast with instructions.

Related PRs: references pr-64000 (values migration spike) and pr-63541 (encryption/tolerations fixes).
